objective: Qualify a bounded multiple-case empirical paper on repair verification boundaries, without claiming new fault categories or ecosystem prevalence.

upstream_test_audit.scope: Seven repair PR change lists across four projects, plus pinned Agno/Hermes test files.
upstream_test_audit.execution: Execute unchanged selected upstream Agno test functions with their original assertion bodies; execute complete upstream Hermes structured-content test modules against three pinned native handlers. Selection and failures recorded. Not the complete project test suites.
upstream_test_audit.selection_rule: Agno tests whose names concern structured content, metadata, or fallback to structured data; Hermes all test methods in the two repair-specific structured-content modules.
upstream_test_audit.interpretation: A passing preservation assertion may be correct for its tested contract while inadequate to establish downstream availability. Failure of an old representation-specific assertion on a later repair is not automatically semantic regression.

provider_request_capture.project: Agno 2.6.20 native Agent and OpenAI-compatible client
provider_request_capture.intervention: Swap only pinned MCP adapter implementation; freeze task, model configuration, tool schema and tool response within each comparison.
provider_request_capture.capture: A loopback HTTP receiver returns a scripted tool call and records the subsequent actual JSON request. It is a transport harness, not an LLM or task-solving baseline.
provider_request_capture.counterfactuals: Two equally shaped records with different required answers per fixture; same question and tool name; check whether actual follow-up request messages distinguish them.
provider_request_capture.claims: Request-level preservation and indistinguishability only; no measured LLM success inferred from scripted replies.

cost: All currently specified executions use local fixtures and loopback HTTP; zero paid model calls.
